sections.h2: Oconee County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Oconee sits in the far west corner of South Carolina, with Georgia on one side and North Carolina on the other. Walhalla is the seat, Seneca is the biggest community, and addresses in Westminster, Keowee Key, Chickasaw Point, Fair Play and Townville come up often too. Population was 78,607 in 2020.

Lakes cover roughly 7% of the county: Hartwell, Keowee and Jocassee. Whether the house is on a county road near Mountain Rest or on Lake Keowee, one set of county offices bills it. Lakefront and hillside parcels bring access and shoreline questions that town lots don't, so ask the county what applies at your address.

Manufacturing supplies 24.8% of jobs. Factory work anchors the housing in town, and the lakes draw a very different kind of owner.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Bills for property other than vehicles are due January 15, following a notice that shows up in the fall. S.C. Code 12-45-70 opens the payment window on September 30. A deadline that falls on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day. For mail, the postmark date is what counts.

Payment optionCost or rule
Card (Discover, MasterCard, Visa), office or online2.35% processing charge
Online e-check$2.00
Delinquent taxesCash, money order or certified funds only; personal and company checks refused

The January 15 deadline falls right after the holidays, so a fall listing should factor it in. Learn the exact bill before a buyer goes under contract, and tell your title company which year is still open.

Go to the Auditor's Office at 415 S. Pine St. in Walhalla, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. To pay, dial 864-638-4162. Questions about notices go to 864-638-4158.

Late charges build in three steps under S.C. Code 12-45-180: 3% right after January 15, then 7% more, then 5% more by March 17. Once March 17 is behind you, the treasurer sends an execution to the delinquent tax officer.

Closing timing can matter here. The law waives penalties when ownership changed during the tax year, the bill went to the previous owner and the buyer never received it in time. Even so, a seller ought to forward any tax mail that turns up after the deed records.

For accounts that go delinquent, the Delinquent Tax Office, 864-638-4147, runs the county's own sale.

sections.h2: The tax sale and your right to redeem
sections.html:
Notice of each sale runs in the Seneca Journal Tribune for three weeks, and only bidders who registered ahead of time may bid. The top bidder wins the property at auction, though the owner keeps one year from the sale date to take it back. The rules sit in S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 51.

Redeeming is open to the owner, to anyone who got the property from the owner, and to a mortgage or judgment creditor. What redeeming costs is the unpaid taxes and fees plus bid-based interest, and the interest rate steps up every three months:

  • Months 1 to 3: 3%
  • Months 4 to 6: 6%
  • Months 7 to 9: 9%
  • Final three months: 12%

A bidder who misses the 4:00 p.m. payment cutoff on sale day owes $500 per parcel. Parcels with no bids go to the Forfeited Land Commission for what is owed. Once a full year passes without redemption, a quitclaim deed usually follows within 30 days.

An objection has to be written, and it has to reach the Assessor inside 90 days of the date shown on the assessment notice. When no notice went out that year, the window stays open until January 15 of the next year.

  1. Your filing lists who you are and how to reach you, the property, why you object, your own fair market value figure and any papers that back it up.
  2. The Assessor reviews it, holds a conference, may inspect the house and answers in writing.
  3. Still unhappy? Within 30 days of the reply, write to the Board of Assessment Appeals at 415 S. Pine St., Walhalla.
  4. Last step: within 30 days of the Board's ruling, ask the Administrative Law Judge Division in Columbia for a hearing.

If the case is unlikely to be settled by December 31, you pay 80% of the tax computed on your proposed value, or you can ask in writing to be billed the full 100%. The result may leave the value alone, lower it or raise it. Questions go to the Assessor, 864-638-4150.

The 4% ratio covers your legal residence plus up to five contiguous acres. S.C. Code 12-43-220 puts all other real property at 6%. Once the 4% ratio is granted, the school tax credit for owner-occupied homes follows automatically.

Renting the house out for more than 72 days in a calendar year ends eligibility. Staying silent after eligibility ends is costly: past six months without telling the Assessor, the statute lets the county charge back the full tax paid, plus 0.5% interest monthly, with a $30 floor.

Picture an owner who left town and leased the house for a year. That house will likely carry the 6% rate, and buyers count the higher bill against the price. The Assessor at 864-638-4150 can tell you which rate sits on your parcel today.

Deed recording runs $1.85 for every $500 of value, with $1.30 going to Columbia and $0.55 staying with the county, per S.C. Code 12-24-10 and 12-24-90.

Under 12-43-217 the county revalues property every fifth year. When a value moves by $1,000 or more, the Assessor mails a notice. The next year on the cycle is a question for that office.

At closing the year's taxes are normally prorated between the two sides. A bill that is still open in January should be cleared from the sale money, which keeps penalties away from the next owner.

sections.h2: If you owe taxes and want to sell
sections.html:
Whatever tax is owed gets paid out of your sale money at the closing table. The sellers we hear about in Oconee County tend to fit one of three profiles: heirs holding a house with years of unpaid tax, owners of a lake or hillside place that needs work before a bank will lend, and landlords tired of a rental.

  • Heirs: ask the Assessor if the 4% rate is still on the house.
  • Anyone behind: call the Delinquent Tax Office at 864-638-4147 before the sale is advertised.
  • Anyone needing speed: a cash buyer closes without waiting for a lender's appraisal.

Hillside and Keowee-side owners often find that the repair list is the real obstacle, not the tax bill. A lender will want the roof, the deck and the shoreline access in good order before it commits, while a cash offer prices the house as it stands.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses in their current condition, so repairs aren't a precondition for an offer. Collect the payoff number from the county, and the offer can be built around that figure.

All four counters are at one address, 415 S. Pine St., Walhalla, so one trip can cover several questions. Payments: 864-638-4162. Notices: 864-638-4158. Assessor: 864-638-4150. Delinquent Tax: 864-638-4147. Take the parcel number or address, photo ID and your closing date, if there is one. Sellers in Seneca or Westminster still drive to Walhalla for most of this, so phone first and confirm the person you need is at the counter that day. Jot down who gave you each answer, then pass the figures to the title company.

faqs.q: What is the Oconee County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: January 15 each year. Notices go out in the fall, and a mailed payment is on time if the postmark beats the deadline.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay my Oconee County bill late?
faqs.a: Penalties of 3%, then 7% more, then 5% more apply by March 17, and after that the account moves to collection.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to contest an Oconee County value?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the date on the notice, in writing, to the Assessor. If no notice was issued that year, you have until January 15 of the next year.

faqs.q: Do I get the house back after a tax sale in Oconee County?
faqs.a: For one year after the sale you can redeem it by paying the taxes, costs and penalties plus 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% interest, depending on the quarter.

faqs.q: Can an Oconee County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The county is paid from your proceeds at closing. Cash Home Buyers can purchase the house as is and sort out the payoff with the county.
